description: This Final Notice refers to breaches of Principle 2 of the FCA’s Principles for Businesses and Article 16(2) of the Market Abuse Regulation related to market protection and wholesale conduct in the Investment Banking and Trading Firm sector. We imposed a financial penalty.
For failing to adequately manage conflicts of interest between itself and its customers as well as systems and controls failings, in relation to the Gold Fixing.
For serious misconduct relating to the Special Liquidity Scheme (SLS), the Repo Rate benchmark and the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
For failing to take reasonable care to organise and control its affairs responsibly and effectively with adequate risk management systems in relation to G10 spot FX voice trading in London.

For breaching Principles 5, 3 and 11 of the Authority's Principles for Businesses.
For breaching Principle 3 of the Authority's Principles for Businesses.

For failing to observe proper standards of market conduct and failing to act with integrity by placing orders to seek to influence the Gold Fixing and for failing to act with integrity for being misleading and untruthful to the FCA and the firm.
For breaches of PRIN 5 and FIT related to benchmarks, lack of fitness/propriety and wholesale conduct in the investment bank sector. We imposed a fine and prohibition.

Guilty plea to conspiracy to defraud (USD LIBOR), Barclays submitter; sentenced 4 years in July 2016. Plea month October 2014; day not published.
Convicted of conspiracy to defraud (USD LIBOR manipulation), former Barclays traders and submitters; sentences 2 years 9 months to 6.5 years.
Convicted of conspiracy to defraud (yen LIBOR), former UBS and Citigroup trader. Conviction quashed by the UK Supreme Court on 23 July 2025. Attributed to UBS, his main employer during the conduct.
Guilty plea to conspiracy to defraud (EURIBOR manipulation 2005-2009), former Deutsche Bank principal trader.
Convicted in absentia of conspiracy to defraud (EURIBOR manipulation), former Barclays trader.

Convicted of conspiracy to defraud (EURIBOR), former Barclays trader; quashed by the UK Supreme Court on 23 July 2025. Same EURIBOR case as Moryoussef, grouped as one event. Day of verdict not published.

Convicted of conspiracy to insider deal (Operation Tabernula), using inside information from his banks' deals 2006-2010; employed by Morgan Stanley, Lehman Brothers and, from 2008, Deutsche Bank. Attributed to Deutsche Bank, the last employer.
Convicted of five counts of insider dealing; senior compliance officer at UBS AG London who passed takeover information to a day trader.
